alerts.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 31 at 10:37AM MDT until November 2 at 12:00PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected above 10, 000 feet. Total snow
accumulations between 12 and 18 inches, with locally higher amounts
possible. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Northwest San Juan Mountains and Southwest San Juan
Mountains.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Sunday to noon MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Monday morning commute.
alerts.areaDesc: Northwestern San Juan Mountains; Southwest San Juan Mountains

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 31 at 9:42AM MDT until November 2 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
...The National Weather Service in Grand Junction CO has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Colorado...

San Juan River at Pagosa Springs affecting Archuleta County.

For the San Juan River...including Pagosa Springs...Major flooding is
forecast.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/gjt.

The next statement will be issued Monday morning at 845 AM MST.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of
record.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Pagosa Springs.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon to Monday evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:00 AM MDT Saturday the stage was 7.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
tomorrow afternoon to a crest of 17.0 feet early Monday morning.
It will then fall below flood stage Monday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 10/05/1911.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 30 at 3:02PM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and southeast
Utah, including the following areas, Canyonlands/Natural Bridges,
La Sal and Abajo Mountains and Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...From late Saturday night through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recently burned areas, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1 to 3 inches of rain is expected across portions of southeast
Utah and southwest Colorado from Sunday morning through Monday
morning over soils that are still saturated from recent rainfall
and flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
alerts.areaDesc: Southwest San Juan Mountains; Four Corners/Upper Dolores River; Animas River Basin; San Juan River Basin; Southeast Utah; La Sal and Abajo Mountains; Canyonlands/Natural Bridges

alerts.title: Paving Operations-150993
alerts.description: Between Frontage Road and Kirk Lane (1 mile east of the Durango area) from Mile Point 88 to Mile Point 92. Right lane closed due to paving operations. Starting Sunday at 7:00PM MDT until Monday, at about 7:00AM MDT. Full schedule below: • November 1, 7:00PM - November 2, 7:00AM Comment: Various eastbound and westbound single lane closures, reduced speed limit to 40 mph and up to 15-minute delays. For more information email: resurfacingproject@gmail.com.

alerts.title: Paving Operations-150998
alerts.description: Between Frontage Road and County Road 232 (near Durango) from Mile Point 88 to Mile Point 89.5. Paving operations. Alternating traffic. Starting Sunday at 7:00PM MDT until Monday, at about 7:00AM MDT. Full schedule below: • November 1, 7:00PM - November 2, 7:00AM Comment: The US 550-US 160 Grandview Interchange exit and entrance ramps will experience staggered nighttime closures from7 p.m. to 7 a.m., Sunday night through Friday morning. Motorists traveling southbound and northbound on US 550 between Durango and New Mexico will detour on Wilson Gulch Drive and Three Springs Boulevard to access the Grandview Bridge and points beyond. For more information email: resurfacingproject@gmail.com.

alerts.title: US 160 Pagosa Springs Reconstruction-147606
alerts.description: Between US 84 and Pike Drive (Pagosa Springs) from Mile Point 144.3 to Mile Point 141.8. Road construction. Starting October 31, 2026 at 7:00AM MDT until October 31, 2026 at about 6:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • October 31, 7:00AM - October 31, 6:00PM Comment: Harman Park & Piedra Road-Work is underway at this intersection of US 160. Working hours will be intermittent day and night so motorists should plan for potential delays, Monday-Saturday. Please allow extra time to get through the work zone. Safety benefits of this work includes pedestrian safety upgrades and ADA accessibility improvements. Expect lane shifts and up to 15-minute delays. Crews will switch two-way traffic into the eastbound lanes, perform temporary striping operations and begin asphalt milling in the westbound lanes. Parking will not be permitted on US 160 and vehicles will be towed at the owner's expense. Westbound lane closures, 10’ width and 75’ length restrictions will remain in place 24/7 through end of 2026. Work is weather-dependent. For questions contact the project team at 970-335-9230 or Pagosa160reconstruction@gmail.com Project Webpage: www.codot.gov/projects/us160pagosasprings
